label: input token f in the first three original positions
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter f during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at an early position, t = 0, 1 or 2. The predicate has precision 1.0 on dev (every f at t<=2 fires) and covers 99.6% of activation mass. Magnitude falls with position: f at t=0 is near max (about 1.73, 43% of mass), t=1 is lower (37%), t=2 lower again (20%), and t=3 gives only weak, occasional activations (about 20% of f at t=3, 0.4% of mass, mostly when f is its first occurrence). It never fires on f at t>=4, on the delimiter, during the copy phase (including when f is fed back or output), or on any token other than f.

issues: The test split matches the reported scores exactly: precision 1.0, recall 0.939, F1 0.968, mass recall 0.996, and 0 false positives.

All 3265 missed test activations are weak (about 0.01-0.10 of max) firings on f at t=3, together 0.4% of activation mass. Targeted scoring of f at t=3 gives precision 0.20, so it fires about 20% of the time, as claimed. The 'mostly the first f' claim is only weak: the firing rate is 0.21 when it is the first f and 0.14 when it is not, and the 'mostly' comes largely from base rates. This is minor.

The phase claims check out. The profile shows 0 activations on the delimiter and in the copy phase. f fed back as input in the copy phase (90,787 test steps) never fires, and no token other than f ever fires.

The magnitude-by-position claims check out (mass share t0 0.43, t1 0.37, t2 0.20, t3 0.004; max 1.727). Rates at t=0..2 are about equal (about 3.3%, roughly the base rate of f). So every f at t<=2 fires, and the decay is in magnitude, not frequency.
No systematic counterexample class remains beyond the documented weak t=3 tail.
